# Exit codes handbook

<!-- Generated by cmd/gen-exit-docs from internal/cliexitdoc/registry.go — do not edit by hand. -->

Client and operator reference for `cisco-aid-cli` exit codes: what each code
means, which commands can return it, and what to do next.

**Canonical contract:** `internal/clierror` (implementation) · [spec 001](specs/001-cli-core/design.md) (summary table)

For CI branching examples, see [getting-started-client.md §6](getting-started-client.md#6-use-exit-codes-in-cicd).

---

## How errors are reported

On any non-zero exit, the CLI prints to **stderr**:

```text
Error: <short message>
Request ID: <id>     # present on API errors when the server returns one
Hint: <remediation>  # when available; policy verdicts (10/20) omit hints
```

Usage errors (exit **2**) also print command help after the error block.

**Stdout vs stderr:** scan and API commands write JSON results to **stdout**.
Pipelines should capture stdout for parsing and check `$?` (or `%ERRORLEVEL%`)
for outcome. Policy verdicts (10/20) still emit scan JSON on stdout before
exiting non-zero.

---

## Exit code summary

| Code | Class | Meaning | Typical action |
|------|-------|---------|----------------|
| **0** | Success | Command completed; policy pass (no findings at/above `--fail-on`) | Continue |
| **1** | Unexpected | Uncategorized or internal failure | Inspect message; file issue if reproducible |
| **2** | Usage | Bad flags/args, client validation, HTTP 400, non-TTY wizard | Fix invocation or run in a terminal |
| **3** | Auth / config | Missing/invalid API key or base URL, HTTP 401/403 | Run `onboard` or fix env/TOML |
| **4** | Network | Timeout, transport failure, poll budget exhausted, HTTP 429/5xx | Retry with backoff; check VPN/CA |
| **5** | Scan failed | Scan FAILED/CANCELED, bad scan id (404), local AIBOM analyzer crash | Verify input/id; re-run scan |
| **10** | Policy fail | Scan **completed**; findings at/above `--fail-on` | Review findings; adjust thresholds if reporting-only |
| **20** | Policy block | Scan **completed**; findings at/above `--block-on` | Review findings; treat as hard stop |

**Design rule:** codes **1–9** mean the tool could not complete the operation.
Codes **≥10** mean the scan finished and a policy gate decided fail/block. CI
pipelines should branch on this distinction.

## Global scenarios (all commands)

These apply to any command that calls the AI Defense API or shares auth resolution.

| Scenario | Code | Hint / notes | Retry? |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| Success | 0 | — | — |
| Invalid flag or Cobra parse error | 2 | Usage printed | No |
| Unknown subcommand / missing required flag | 2 | Usage printed | No |
| Client-side validation (`ValidationError`) | 2 | Fix arguments | No |
| Missing API key or base URL | 3 | `Run 'cisco-aid-cli onboard'…` | No |
| Base URL host not `*.cisco.com` | 3 | Use a regional endpoint | No |
| HTTP 400 from API | 2 | Check command arguments | No |
| HTTP 401 / 403 | 3 | Check API key and tenant region | No |
| HTTP 404 (bad scan/server/BOM id) | 5 | Verify id belongs to your tenant | No |
| HTTP 429 or 5xx | 4 | Rate limit or transient outage | **Yes** |
| DNS / TLS / connection refused / request timeout | 4 | VPN, proxy, `SSL_CERT_FILE` | **Yes** |
| Scan poll budget exhausted | 4 | Increase retry env vars (see below) | **Yes** |
| Unclassified error | 1 | — | Maybe |

### Poll timeout environment variables

| Scan type | Variables |
|-----------|-----------|
| Model scan | `AI_DEFENSE_RETRY_COUNT_FOR_SCANNING`, `AI_DEFENSE_WAIT_TIME_SECS_SUCCESSIVE_SCAN_INFO_CHECK` |
| MCP scan | `AI_DEFENSE_MCP_RETRY_COUNT`, `AI_DEFENSE_MCP_WAIT_TIME_SECS` |

## Policy gating (`--fail-on` / `--block-on`)

Applies to: `model-scan trigger`, `model-scan info`, `mcp-scan run`,
`mcp-scan info --scan-id`.

Does **not** apply to: `mcp-scan info --server-id`, `ai-bom`, `config`,
`install`, `onboard`, list/delete/register commands.

| Flag | Default | Disable |
|------|---------|---------|
| `--fail-on` | `low` | `--fail-on none` (also `off`, `never`) |
| `--block-on` | `critical` | `--block-on none` |

| Outcome | Code |
|---------|------|
| No findings at/above `--fail-on` | 0 |
| Findings ≥ `--fail-on`, below `--block-on` | 10 |
| Findings ≥ `--block-on` | 20 |

Gate summary on stderr (no hint): `model-scan: scan decision FAIL (highest severity HIGH, 3 finding(s))`

Report findings without failing the step: `--fail-on none --block-on none`.

## Non-TTY quick reference

| Command | Without a terminal |
|---------|-------------------|
| `onboard`, `config init`, `config profile create`, `config edit` | Exit **2** (usage) |
| `config show` | Plain redacted TOML (exit **0** unless load fails) |
| Scan / API commands | Unchanged |

## CI/CD cheat sheet

```bash
cisco-aid-cli model-scan trigger -f ./model.pth --fail-on high
case $? in
  0)  echo "clean" ;;
  10) echo "findings at/above fail threshold"; exit 1 ;;
  20) echo "blocked at/above block threshold"; exit 1 ;;
  4)  echo "transient — retry"; exit 75 ;;
  3)  echo "fix credentials"; exit 1 ;;
  *)  echo "scan could not run"; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

| Goal | Approach |
|------|----------|
| Fail pipeline on findings | Default `--fail-on` / `--block-on` (or stricter) |
| Report only, never fail on findings | `--fail-on none --block-on none` |
| Distinguish infra vs findings | Branch on `10`/`20` vs `1`–`5` |
| Parse unified verdict JSON | Add `--envelope` |

## Keeping this document accurate

**Do not edit this file by hand.** Update `internal/cliexitdoc/registry.go` when command
exit behavior changes, then run:

```bash
make gen-exit-docs
```

CI runs `make check-exit-docs` to ensure the handbook matches the registry.

1. Update command handlers and `internal/clierror` if needed.
2. Add or change rows in `internal/cliexitdoc/registry.go`.
3. Run `make gen-exit-docs` and commit the diff.
4. Update [spec 001](specs/001-cli-core/design.md) summary table if codes changed.
5. Note user-visible changes in [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).

Spec requirements: **REQ-D04**, **REQ-D05** in [specs/001-cli-core/requirements.md](specs/001-cli-core/requirements.md).
